| [CASE-133](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-133.md) v2 | American party realignment: each major party kept its name and organizational continuity across the twentieth century while its coalition and its stance on civil rights changed, and the change began in state parties, unions and constituencies before it reached national leaders | The owner's case at U29 and U30 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, in the replies' corrected form. | [CASE-136](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-136.md) v5 | The doorway effect: memory for an object carried through a doorway into another room is worse than after walking as far within one, returning to the first room does not restore it, and outside the original laboratory's set-up the effect has not always appeared | The owner's case at U37 of the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, offered as one the record's account of perspective and grounding may at least partly explain. | [CASE-137](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-137.md) v3 | Clive Wearing: a musician left by encephalitis with almost no memory of his past and none of the last minutes, who still plays, sight-reads and conducts, keeps his attachment to his wife, and writes over and over that he has just become conscious for the first time | The owner's case, proposed at U26 of the exchange of 2026-10-22 ("if we haven't already examined the case of Clive Wearing, that might be another good addition"). | [CASE-138](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-138.md) v3 | Challenger to Columbia: NASA corrected its launch decisions and its safety organization after 1986, and the Columbia board found in 2003 that related organizational failure mechanisms had recurred, while its lessons-learned system was little used in between | The owner's case at U25 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: NASA's mechanisms for documenting and learning from mistakes, with Challenger as the classic example. Not shown: why the correction decayed, which [THEORY-140](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md) explains and this case only displays. | Active |
| [CASE-139](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-139.md) v2 | Chinese martial traditions through the Cultural Revolution: practices restricted, teachers persecuted and teaching driven underground, then after 1978 a reconstruction of Shaolin martial arts through heritage policy and tourism in which local practitioners and authorized institutions dispute who carries the tradition | The owner's case at U37 of the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the "(various) perspectival interruption(s) caused by the Chinese Cultural Revolution", near the record's martial-arts material ([CASE-130](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-130.md)). | [CASE-140](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-140.md) v2 | The attributed self: two people with similar dispositions hear the same negative characterization, one told it comes from a few critics and the other believing it speaks for nearly everyone who matters to them, so that the words are fixed and only their attributed breadth differs | A39's proposed test of the imagined audience, in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request. A39: "These cases distinguish the content of a judgment from the social authority attributed to it." As stipulated it predicts nothing; run with real people, it would test [CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md). | Active |
| [CASE-141](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-141.md) v2 | The label that confirms itself: a pupil wrongly labelled disruptive is watched more closely, ordinary conduct is read as misconduct, the pupil's frustration produces real misconduct, and the label looks justified in hindsight | A39's second reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request with its variant [CASE-142](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-142.md). A39: "Here an interpretive regime partially manufactures the evidence it uses to justify itself." | [CASE-143](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-143.md) v2 | Franklin's borrowed book: Benjamin Franklin, opposed by a new member of the Pennsylvania Assembly when he stood again as its clerk, asked to borrow a rare book from him rather than courting him, returned it with thanks, and found the man civil and later a friend | The owner's U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", read at U2 as a "perspectival invitation". | [CASE-144](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-144.md) v5 | The evaluator that stops tracking: two populations of specialists with identical capabilities and task streams, one scored against independent outcomes and one by an evaluator that weights evidence agreeing with its previously favoured specialists, after a shift that makes a marginalized specialist uniquely competent | Proposed in the exchange of 2026-10-23, "Framework Overview Request", at A5 (section 5) with A4's "corrigibility trap", after the owner asked which experiments could "kill multiple birds with one stone" (U4) and which questions simulation could answer (U5). Not run. | Active |

| [CASE-146](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-146.md) v3 | Two friendships across a group line: in one, the friend becomes an exception and the person's view of the friend's group is unchanged; in the other, what happens with the friend changes how the person takes other members of the group, though the friendships are alike in warmth and in what each learns | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained", A4 and A5, on the owner's U4 about intergroup contact. | [CASE-151](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md) | Wells Fargo's Community Bank, 2002–2016: unauthorized and unwanted accounts that the board's own investigation traced to the sales model, the performance management that enforced it and a decentralized structure, while signals of the harm reached people who could not act on them | The Wells Fargo sales-practices episode, as reported by the bank's independent directors (2017; [LIT-1425](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1425.md), read in [NOTE-1095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1095.md)). | [CASE-159](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-159.md) v2 | Authority geometry and response geometry: when an organization's response is the authority-weighted mixture p_π(y \| c) = Σ πᵢ pᵢ(y \| c), the Fisher metric of its responses is the pullback JᵀD⁻¹J of the categorical (Shahshahani) metric on the shares π and never exceeds it; it vanishes along any redistribution between processes that respond alike under the probes used, so two specialists who both answer yes with probability 0.8 in routine contexts carry no information about their shares there, while a rare context in which they answer 0.9 and 0.1 carries 0.64/(p(1 − p)) per observation, p = 0.1 + 0.8π | From the continuation of the exchange of 2026-10-24 (U28–U31), where it appears in four replies (A28 §3, A29's second priority, A30 §6A and A31's probe diagnostic); checked when filed. What an evaluator sees is the response mixture, whose Fisher metric is that metric pulled back through the processes' response profiles. The mixture counterpart of [CASE-152](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-152.md)'s product model. | Active |
